bugs.summary: manifestReadProblem accepts a held-out manifest that carries a sealed block but has lost its custody field. The custody guards then treat that manifest as giving no live-sharer protection while still counting its bundle digest as accounted for, so a pending reseal can be hidden and release or rekey can go ahead against the predecessor set and expose content it shares.

seal --from-backup checks whether the source backup already belongs to another set only against sealed/backups.json on main, before decrypting, and the custody transaction records no source-backup digest. Two checkouts can therefore seal the same backup under two set names before either registry entry reaches main, and both succeed, giving identical held-out tasks two independent opening budgets.

The new binding that records a seal's source backup in the custody log is enforced only by seal.ts. bindBackups, which rekey and compare-backups share, still binds a backup by sealed/backups.json on main alone, so --declare-backup can bind a backup the custody log already records as another set's seal source, and rekey can then re-encrypt that other set's held-out content to an outside recipient.
